title: 4. Dissolution
subtitle: Dissolution of Partnership vs Dissolution of Firm, Modes of Dissolution, Settlement of Accounts, Accounting Entries

questions.q: "Dissolution of partnership" refers to a situation where:
options: The firm is converted into a private limited company
The firm's business comes to a complete end
All partners are declared insolvent
The mutual relationship between some partners changes but the firm continues

questions.q: "Dissolution of a firm" refers to a situation where:
options: A new partner is admitted
The partnership deed is merely amended
The relationship between all partners comes to an end and the firm's business ceases
Only one partner retires while the business continues

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of dissolution of partnership, without necessarily dissolving the firm?
options: Completion of the specific venture for which the firm was formed, with no renewal
Admission, retirement, or death of a partner, where the business continues
Expiry of the fixed term for which the firm was constituted, with no renewal
Insolvency of all partners

questions.q: Dissolution of a firm by agreement means:
options: The firm automatically dissolves after five years
One partner alone decides to dissolve the firm without consent
A court orders dissolution
All partners mutually agree to dissolve the firm

questions.q: Compulsory dissolution of a firm occurs, among other situations, when:
options: One partner wishes to retire
A new partner is admitted
All partners, or all but one partner, become insolvent
The firm earns a loss in a particular year

questions.q: A partnership at will may be dissolved by:
options: Only by a court order
Only after the firm completes ten years of operation
Any partner giving notice in writing to all other partners of their intention to dissolve the firm
Only with government permission

questions.q: Dissolution of a firm by the Court may be ordered, under the Indian Partnership Act, on grounds such as:
options: A partner asking for a salary increase
Minor disagreements over day-to-day expenses
A partner taking a short leave of absence
A partner's unsound mind, permanent incapacity, or misconduct affecting the business

questions.q: Which of the following would make a partnership's business unlawful, leading to compulsory dissolution?
options: A decline in the firm's annual profit
A partner's marriage
A subsequent change in law making the firm's business illegal
A partner's temporary illness

questions.q: On dissolution of a firm, a Realisation Account is prepared mainly to:
options: Record only partners' drawings
Record only the firm's sales for the year
Record the sale/realisation of assets and payment of liabilities, and ascertain profit or loss on dissolution
Record the admission of a new partner

questions.q: On dissolution, assets other than cash/bank are transferred to the Realisation Account by:
options: Crediting the Partners' Capital Accounts
Crediting the Realisation Account and debiting the respective asset accounts
Debiting the Partners' Capital Accounts
Debiting the Realisation Account and crediting the respective asset accounts

questions.q: On dissolution, outside liabilities are transferred to the Realisation Account by:
options: Debiting the Realisation Account and crediting the respective liability accounts
Crediting the Realisation Account and debiting the respective liability accounts
Crediting the Partners' Capital Accounts
Debiting the Partners' Capital Accounts

questions.q: When an asset is taken over by a partner on dissolution, the accounting entry is:
options: Debit the Realisation Account, credit the partner's Capital Account
Debit Cash/Bank, credit the Realisation Account
Debit the Realisation Account, credit Cash/Bank
Debit the partner's Capital Account, credit the Realisation Account

questions.q: When a partner agrees to personally discharge a firm's liability on dissolution, the accounting entry is:
options: Debit the Realisation Account, credit Cash/Bank
Debit the Realisation Account, credit the partner's Capital Account
Debit the partner's Capital Account, credit the Realisation Account
Debit Cash/Bank, credit the partner's Capital Account

questions.q: Expenses incurred on dissolution (realisation expenses) are generally:
options: Debited directly to the Partners' Capital Accounts in every case, bypassing the Realisation Account
Debited to the Realisation Account
Credited to the Realisation Account
Ignored in the firm's final accounts

questions.q: As per Section 48 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, losses, including deficiencies of capital, are paid first out of:
options: The senior-most partner's personal assets only
Profits, next out of capital, and lastly, if necessary, by the partners individually in their profit-sharing ratio
The firm's goodwill only
Government compensation

questions.q: As per Section 48, the assets of the firm (including sums contributed by partners to make up a deficiency) are generally applied in the order:
options: Government dues, then third-party debts, then partners
Firm's debts to third parties, then partners' loans, then partners' capitals, then any surplus to partners in profit-sharing ratio
Partners' capitals first, then third-party debts, then partners' loans
Equally to all claimants regardless of type

questions.q: On dissolution, loans given by a partner to the firm (as distinct from capital) are:
options: Repaid after outside creditors but before partners' capital balances are settled
Never repaid, as they are treated as capital
Repaid before outside creditors
Repaid simultaneously with partners' capital, with no priority

questions.q: If the Realisation Account shows a loss on dissolution, it is shared by the partners in their:
options: Equal ratio, irrespective of the profit-sharing ratio in the deed
Capital ratio, irrespective of profit-sharing ratio
Profit-sharing ratio
Gaining ratio

questions.q: On dissolution, the final step after settling the Realisation Account and all liabilities is to:
options: Prepare a fresh Balance Sheet for the dissolved firm
Admit a new partner
Close the Partners' Capital Accounts by paying off the balances due to them
Revalue the firm's goodwill for the last time

questions.q: Dissolution of partnership, without dissolution of the firm, typically happens upon:
options: A change in the constitution of the firm, such as admission or retirement, while the business continues
Court-ordered closure of the business
Sale of the entire business to an outside party
Winding up of all the firm's affairs

questions.q: Under Section 44 of the Indian Partnership Act, a court may order dissolution of a firm on the application of a partner if another partner:
options: Has taken an extra day of leave
Has asked for a bonus
Has suggested a new product line
Is found to be of unsound mind

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a mode of dissolution recognised under the Indian Partnership Act?
options: Automatic dissolution after exactly three years, regardless of any agreement or event
Compulsory dissolution
Dissolution by court order
Dissolution by agreement

questions.q: A firm constituted for a fixed term is, subject to contract between the partners, dissolved:
options: Never, unless all partners die
Only by a court order
Only when the firm is converted into a company
On the expiry of that fixed term

questions.q: A firm constituted to carry out one or more specific adventures or undertakings is dissolved:
options: On the completion of that adventure or undertaking
Only after 20 years
Only by compulsory liquidation
Only by mutual retirement of all partners

questions.q: On dissolution, unrecorded assets realised in cash are:
options: Ignored, since they were never recorded
Credited directly to the Partners' Capital Accounts
Debited to the Realisation Account and credited to Cash/Bank
Debited to Cash/Bank and credited to the Realisation Account

questions.q: On dissolution, unrecorded liabilities paid off are:
options: Debited directly to the Partners' Capital Accounts
Debited to the Realisation Account and credited to Cash/Bank
Ignored, since they were never recorded
Credited to the Realisation Account and debited to Cash/Bank

questions.q: If a solvent partner's Capital Account shows a debit balance on dissolution (the partner owes the firm), that amount is:
options: Ignored entirely
Transferred to the Goodwill Account
Automatically written off as a firm loss
Paid by the partner to the firm

questions.q: Dissolution of a firm by notice applies specifically to:
options: A partnership at will
A partnership for a fixed term
A partnership formed for a single specific venture
A partnership where all partners are companies

questions.q: Goodwill appearing in the Balance Sheet at the time of dissolution is treated by:
options: Treating it as a liability
Retaining it permanently in the books
Transferring it directly to the Partners' Capital Accounts without passing through Realisation
Transferring it to the Realisation Account along with other assets

questions.q: The closing cash/bank balance after dissolution, once all liabilities are paid and partners settled, should ideally be:
options: Equal to the original capital of the firm
Equal to the firm's total goodwill
Nil
A fixed statutory amount

questions.q: If the firm's assets realise more than their book value on dissolution, the surplus represents:
options: A liability to outside creditors
Goodwill
Profit on realisation, credited to the Realisation Account
A loss on realisation

questions.q: If the firm's assets realise less than their book value on dissolution, the shortfall represents:
options: A liability to be paid by creditors
Profit on realisation
An increase in partners' capital
Loss on realisation, debited to the Realisation Account

questions.q: A partner's private estate, under the Indian Partnership Act, is applied after dissolution first towards:
options: The firm's debts exclusively, before any private debts
Nothing; private estates are never touched
Equal division between all creditors, private and firm, with no order of priority
That partner's own private debts, with any surplus applied towards firm debts

questions.q: The firm's property, after dissolution, is applied first towards:
options: Government taxes exclusively
Equal division between firm and private creditors
The firm's debts to third parties, in priority over any private debts of partners
A partner's private debts first

questions.q: Which of the following is a ground for compulsory dissolution of a firm?
options: All partners, or all but one, becoming insolvent
One partner going on a long vacation
A partner opening a personal savings account
A fall in the firm's sales for one quarter

questions.q: On dissolution, any undistributed balance of the Profit and Loss Account appearing in the Balance Sheet is:
options: Transferred to the Partners' Capital Accounts in the profit-sharing ratio, before preparing the Realisation Account
Ignored entirely
Transferred to the Realisation Account
Transferred to the firm's creditors

questions.q: A Garner vs Murray type situation (deficiency of an insolvent partner) can arise on dissolution when:
options: One or more partners are unable to pay the amount due from them on settlement of accounts
A new partner is admitted during dissolution
All partners are solvent and pay promptly
The firm earns a large profit on realisation

questions.q: Dissolution accounting is distinct from accounting for admission or retirement mainly because dissolution involves:
options: Only adjusting the profit-sharing ratio
Only admitting a replacement partner
Closing all accounts of the firm permanently, since the business ceases to exist
Only revaluing assets without any sale

questions.q: "Settlement of accounts" on dissolution, as governed by Section 48, is a default rule that applies:
options: Only when a court orders dissolution
In the absence of a contrary agreement between the partners
Only to firms registered after 1932
Only when the firm has fewer than three partners

questions.q: Dissolution of a firm formed for a particular venture, once that venture is complete, differs from a partnership at will in that:
options: It requires the consent of outside creditors
It can never be dissolved
It requires a court order in every case
It dissolves automatically on completion of the venture, without any notice being required
